title: Lesson 7: Spiritual Warfare and Putting on the Armor of God
description: The Christian life is not a stroll through a quiet park. It is a battle, and you are already in it. This lesson will help you understand the real enemy you face, the armor God has given you, and how to stand firm every single day.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw how to live for Jesus at work and school. Here is something every believer needs to hear clearly: living on mission will meet resistance. Not just from a busy schedule or an awkward conversation, but from a real spiritual enemy who hates what God is doing in you and through you. This lesson is about the battle you are already in, and the armor God has already given you to stand firm.
Sent into the Battle

blocks.title: Jesus Sends the 72
blocks.text: Before Paul ever wrote about the armor of God, Jesus sent His followers into a real spiritual battle. In Luke 10, Jesus sent seventy-two of His followers out on mission, two by two. He told them to carry nothing extra, to speak peace over every house they entered, and to proclaim that the kingdom of God had come near. They went in His name, with His authority, and with nothing but trust in what He had told them. When they came back, they were amazed at what had happened.

The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!" And he said to them, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you. Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

Look at what Jesus does here. His followers just experienced real spiritual victory. Demons submitted to them. And Jesus does not say "good job." He says, "Do not rejoice in this." Instead, rejoice that your names are written in heaven. He is pointing them away from the power they felt and toward the identity they already had. That is the heart of spiritual warfare. You are not fighting to earn a place with God. You are fighting from the place He has already given you.
7.1 - When have you felt real spiritual resistance while trying to follow Jesus or serve others?
Dress for the Battle You Are Already In

Years later, the apostle Paul gave the church a fuller picture of what Jesus' followers were already living. Writing as a prisoner in chains (Ephesians 6:20), perhaps with a Roman soldier close by, Paul described the spiritual equipment God provides for every believer.

Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places. Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand firm. Stand therefore, having fastened on the belt of truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and, as shoes for your feet, having put on the readiness given by the gospel of peace. In all circumstances, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one; and take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication.

Notice what Paul does not say. He does not say "go find some armor." He says "put on the whole armor of God." This is not a "try harder" speech. It is a "be dependent" command. The armor is not something you manufacture. It is something God supplies. Your job is to put it on. Walk through the diagram below and watch each piece appear. Pay attention to the key line for each one. These are the words you will want to remember.
The Six Pieces of Armor

The Belt of Truth. Ancient soldiers tucked their robes into their belts so they could move without tripping. If you are not grounded in the truth of the gospel, you will trip over the lies of the world. The enemy's oldest strategy is deception, and he still twists God's words today. The belt of truth means you know what is true about God and about yourself, and you build your life on that foundation instead of on feelings, fears, or the noise around you.

The Breastplate of Righteousness. The breastplate covers your heart, but it is not the breastplate of your good behavior. It is Christ's righteousness. You learned this in Growing Deep with the Grace and Mercy Cycle: Jesus took your sin and gave you His perfect record. When the enemy whispers that you are a fraud or a failure, you point to the breastplate. It is not yours. It is His. And it holds.

The Shoes of the Gospel of Peace. Good shoes let a soldier hold his ground and move where he is sent. Because you have peace with God through Jesus, you can stand steady when the ground shifts underneath you. Peace is not just comfort for your soul. It keeps your feet planted, and it moves you out on mission.
7.2 - Of the belt, the breastplate, and the shoes, which do you most often forget to put on?

The Shield of Faith. A Roman soldier carried a large shield that could cover nearly his whole body. The enemy fires darts at you: doubt, fear, shame, temptation, discouragement. These are mostly thoughts: "It is not worth it. God has forgotten you. You will never change." Faith does not mean you never feel those arrows. It means you hold up the shield and let the truth of God's promises put the fire out.

The Helmet of Salvation. The helmet protects your mind, and the battle for your day is won or lost in what you believe about your security in Christ. When you put on the helmet, you are reminding yourself that you belong to God, that nothing can separate you from His love, and that your future is sealed. Remember what Jesus told the seventy-two: rejoice that your names are written in heaven. That is the helmet.

The Sword of the Spirit. This is the only offensive weapon in the list. Every other piece is for defense. The sword is the Word of God. When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, He did not debate the devil or rely on willpower. He said, "It is written." Three times the devil attacked. Three times Jesus answered with Scripture. You do not fight lies with feelings. You fight lies with truth. But you cannot draw the sword if you do not carry it. This is why knowing your Bible matters so deeply.
7.3 - Which piece of armor do you need most right now?
Stand Together in Prayer

Paul does not stop at the sword. He goes straight on to prayer: "praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication. To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints" (Ephesians 6:18). Prayer is how you put the armor on, and it keeps you connected to the God who supplies every piece.

Notice too who Paul is talking to. Every "you" in this passage is plural. He wrote to a church, not to a lone soldier, and he even asked them to pray that he would speak the gospel boldly (Ephesians 6:19). You were never meant to stand alone. Pray for the believers around you by name, and let them pray for you. When one of you is under fire, the others stand close.
Stand Firm

Paul uses the word stand four times in this passage. Stand against the schemes. Withstand in the evil day. Having done all, stand firm. Stand therefore. The armor of God is not about becoming a spiritual superhero. It is about daily dependence on a God who has already won the war. You are not fighting alone, and you are not fighting for an uncertain outcome. Jesus has already triumphed. The Lord who sent out the seventy-two and told them to rejoice that their names are written in heaven is the same Lord who sends you. Your call is simply to stand.
This Week's Practice

Each morning this week, before you check your phone, pray through the armor one piece at a time: Lord, I put on the belt of Your truth. I put on the breastplate of Christ's righteousness, not my own. Keep going through the shoes, the shield, the helmet, and the sword. It takes about two minutes. Then choose one lie you hear often and memorize one verse that answers it. That verse is your sword for the week.

blocks.title: A Sword for the Lie
content: "God has forgotten you." "I will never leave you nor forsake you" (Hebrews 13:5).
"You will never change." "He who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6).
"You are a fraud and a failure." "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1).

blocks.text: Lesson 7 Review

Living on mission meets real spiritual resistance, but you do not fight to earn a place with God. You fight from the place He has already given you. God supplies the whole armor: the belt of truth, the breastplate of Christ's righteousness, the shoes of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is His Word. You put it on in prayer, and you stand together with other believers. Jesus has already won, so your call is simply to stand.
In the next lesson, you will learn how to walk alongside someone else and help them grow as a follower of Jesus.
